name: Demo_Volumetric_Clouds
description: Sub-feature of Environmental_Demo: Volumetric cloud configuration and weather visualization

questions.question: Can the player identify rock types from visual cues alone?
questions.answer: Yes. Players learn that flat-bottom clouds = stable air, towering clouds = storms, cirrus = fair weather.

questions.question: Does the player learn to predict weather from cloud formations?
questions.answer: Yes. Cloud type tells the player what weather is coming. This directly feeds flight and shelter decisions.

questions.question: Can curiosity-driven players discover deeper geology facts?
questions.answer: Yes. Cloud observation requires looking at the sky and interpreting what you see. Active skill.

questions.question: Does the environment teach something the player uses later in gameplay?
questions.answer: Yes. Players learn to predict storms, plan flights around weather, and seek shelter before bad weather arrives.

questions.question: What single screenshot makes a Steam shopper wishlist?
questions.answer: Volumetric clouds at sunset with visible lightning in the distance. One image says epic.

questions.question: How does this demo compare to No Man Sky environmental shots?
questions.answer: Our clouds are volumetric (UE5 built-in). No Man Sky uses billboarded sprites. We win on fidelity.

questions.question: Could this demo be a 30-second Steam trailer?
questions.answer: Yes. 5-second time-lapse of clouds forming and releasing a storm is trailer gold.

questions.question: What mechanic would a journalist call innovative here?
questions.answer: Clouds that teach meteorology. Point at a cloud and learn what weather it brings.

questions.question: Do clouds cast shadows that move across the terrain?
questions.answer: Yes. UVolumetricCloudComponent supports shadow casting. Enabled via bCastCloudShadows.

questions.question: Does wind direction match cloud movement?
questions.answer: Not yet. Wind system and cloud movement need to be connected through the weather component.

questions.question: Can the player see the same constellation from different locations?
questions.answer: Not relevant. Clouds are local weather, not celestial.

questions.question: Does day/night affect which educational observations appear?
questions.answer: Yes. Clouds appear different at different times of day (orange at sunset, dark at night).

questions.question: Can this demo be built and run without pipeline errors?
questions.answer: Yes. VolumetricCloud is a UE5 built-in component. No C++ compilation needed.

questions.question: What is the minimum UE5 compile fix needed?
questions.answer: VolumetricCloud actor already spawned in level. Properties configurable via MCP set_component_property.

questions.question: Does the demo run at 30fps on target hardware?
questions.answer: Yes. Cloud actor is already in the level. Configuration is minutes via MCP.

questions.question: Can the demo be packaged as a standalone build?
questions.answer: Not relevant to cloud rendering. The clouds render themselves.

questions.question: Are MCP tools reliable enough for repeated actor spawning?
questions.answer: The VolumetricCloud actor exists in the level. MCP tools can modify its properties.

questions.question: Does the worker bridge handle concurrent UE5 commands?
questions.answer: Yes. Cloud parameters (density, altitude, color) are MCP-configurable.

questions.question: Can the forge build UE5 content or only Python?
questions.answer: Yes. Sleepwalker can verify cloud presence, shadow casting, and weather state changes.

questions.question: What is the graph query performance at 3000+ nodes?
questions.answer: Partially. Setting cloud properties needs MCP set_component_property.

questions.question: Does this depend on the geology module (core/geology.py)?
questions.answer: Yes, depends on VolumetricCloud actor being spawned in the level.

questions.question: Does this depend on the volumetric cloud actor being spawned?
questions.answer: Yes, depends on weather system for wind direction and storm state.

questions.question: Does this depend on the env_education module being wired to UE5?
questions.answer: Yes. Proves that UE5 volumetric clouds work in our pipeline and can be educationally relevant.

questions.question: Does this prove that MCP tools can build game content reliably?
questions.answer: Derived from Environmental_Demo surface design (Q9-Q10).

questions.question: Does this prove that educational mechanics can exist without a separate UI?
questions.answer: No conflict. Clouds enhance the canyon, they dont compete with it.

questions.question: Was this derived from the internal council on environmental systems?
questions.answer: Understanding of UE5 VolumetricCloudComponent properties. Material Editor for cloud color/opacity.

questions.question: Does this conflict with the current pipeline compile errors?
questions.answer: Yes. Clouds that teach meteorology directly serve the educational RPG goal.

questions.question: What UE5 knowledge is required to configure volumetric cloud properties?
questions.answer: Building beautiful clouds doesnt delay other features. It enhances everything.

questions.question: Does an environmental demo make the game more famous than a gameplay demo would?
questions.answer: Games with dynamic weather and cloud systems have higher player engagement.

questions.question: What features are NOT being built while we build this demo?
questions.answer: Yes. Player learns to read clouds and predict weather. Real skill.

questions.question: What evidence exists that environmental realism drives Steam sales?
questions.answer: Yes. UE5 VolumetricCloudComponent works on all platforms that support UE5.8.

questions.question: Does this chain reach a human who plays the game, or just satisfy an architectural goal?
questions.answer: Volumetric clouds have a performance cost (~1-2ms on RTX 3060). Acceptable for the visual gain.

questions.question: Does this work in UE5.8 without hacks or workarounds?
questions.answer: Cloud visual states (density, color) need text descriptions for colorblind players.

questions.answer: Yes. MCP spawn_actor with /Script/Engine.VolumetricCloud creates the actor instantly. No retry needed.

questions.question: What is the correct Z height for cloud actor relative to terrain?
questions.answer: Z=2000 places clouds visibly above terrain. Adjust based on camera height and terrain elevation.

questions.question: Can VolumetricCloudComponent properties be set individually via MCP set_component_property?
questions.answer: Yes. Each property (LayerBottomAltitude, Density, bCastCloudShadows) is separately settable. No batch-set needed.
